clue.text: That's the attractive girl I saw! Is it the scullery-maid?

parts.words: That's the attractive girl I saw!
parts.note: surface reading: a man pointing out a pretty girl he spotted earlier
setter's reading: the girl's slang name, a past-tense verb and a pronoun run together make the job title of a kitchen servant

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly points out a pretty girl, and a friend asks whether she is only the kitchen maid.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'that's the dish I saw' as 'DISH WAS HER': a dish is slang for an attractive girl, and the three words run together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery-maid's main task was washing up pots and plates, so she is a person who cleans crockery.

clue.text: Carriage from French electrified railway

parts.note: de is the French word for from
a live wire or rail carries current
standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A train carriage is supplied by a French electric railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage can mean the conveying of goods, as in a charge for postage and carriage, which is what a delivery is.

clue.text: Annoying person's kid collecting a medal

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so the word for kid holds the next piece

parts.note: a kid is a child, here a male one
taken as written
the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: An irritating person's child is picking up a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside SON to give SOAN, then DSO follows; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a mild insult used for an irritating individual instead of a ruder word.

clue.text: Groom stood around to pass bride's first course

indicators.note: around says the two-part phrase for stood sits on either side of what follows

parts.note: someone who stood was up, on their feet
to hand something is to pass it over

indicators.note: the first of the word bride means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of bride
a rush is a swift flow or course of water

explanation.surface: At a wedding, the groom stands about waiting to hand the bride the first course of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-word phrase for stood is split, its halves going either side of the rest. 'Groom' looks like the bridegroom in the scene, but it means a spell of tidying oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick wash and brush-up is a spell of tidying one's appearance, just as to groom oneself is to smarten up.

clue.text: Legislator turns up, not tense but a little nervous

not this but that swaps one letter out and puts another in its place

parts.note: opening letter of nervous

explanation.surface: A lawmaker shows up, not tense, just slightly jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: The second T of ROTATES becomes N, giving ROTANES, which reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an upper chamber that makes laws.

clue.text: Make amends for Windows version 8 in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the words are to be heard said, not read off the page

parts.note: XP was a version of Microsoft Windows, followed by the number eight

explanation.surface: Someone apologises in a talk for the Windows 8 operating system.
explanation.walkthrough: Windows XP and Windows 8 were both real releases; saying 'XP eight' gives ex-pee-ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a wrong is to atone for it or pay the penalty, which is making amends.

clue.text: Swagger about in costume

parts.note: to swagger is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone struts around showing off in fancy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing of a distinctive kind, so it matches outfit or costume.

clue.text: A bit upset in phenomenal bloomer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemone is a flowering plant, and a bloomer in crossword terms is anything that blooms.

clue.text: Sit on judge's carpet

explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to call them in and reprimand them, which is to scold or berate them.

clue.text: Conservative nosedive maybe involves bit of intrigue after a party member's endless plotting

a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

indicators.note: a bit of the word intrigue is just its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of intrigue

explanation.surface: A Conservative slump in the polls involves some intrigue after a Tory's endless scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' appears in the surface and also hides in 'party member', so the clue uses the party twice in different forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiratorial describes the manner of people secretly scheming together, so it means plotting.

clue.text: Affair in Australia is ongoing

clue.text: Heads of vineyard outlets don't keep any spirit

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear distilled alcoholic drink, and spirit is the general term for such liquor.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' wants to be a fashion model; it is the Model T car. 'Took off' looks like undressing but means fled.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferry is to carry people or goods from place to place, which is to transport them.

clue.text: About to ask judge leaving club how to get father out of the RAF

definitions.text: how to get father out of the RAF

indicators.note: the club abbreviation leaves, meaning it is taken out of the judge word

parts.note: a recorder is a part-time judge in the English courts
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A man asks a judge after leaving his club how to get his dad discharged from the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: put the letters of THE RAF in a new order and they spell FATHER. 'About to ask' gives the same word again: RE (about) + ORDER (ask).
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the six letters of the RAF yields a parent's name, so arranging differently is the method.

parts.note: taken as written
